title: Americans Are Increasingly Pessimistic About Avoiding the Worst Effects of Climate Change
summary: About six-in-ten Americans say countries around the world, including the U.S., will not do enough to avoid the worst effects of climate change. This growing pessimism is driven by Democrats.

title: Americans on what causes climate change: Human activity or natural patterns?
summary: Key takeaways: Almost all climate scientists say the planet is warming, and that this is caused mostly by human activity. But a far smaller share of the American public has shared this view over the last decade. title: Do Americans think extreme weather is worse today than in the past?
summary: Key takeaways: Recent scientific studies have found that extreme weather is becoming both more common and more intense, and many Americans have noticed. title: Worldwide, a quarter of new car sales are electric vehicles or hybrids
summary: In eight countries, at least half of all new cars sold in 2025 were electric or hybrid. The U.S. reached just 10%, well below the global average of 25%.

title: In several European countries, EU gets more positive ratings today than during Brexit vote
summary: EU favorability has risen across Europe since the 2016 Brexit vote, with a median of 62% now viewing the organization positively.

title: What Political Issues Do Americans Hear About in Church?
summary: Most U.S. adults who go to religious services say they’ve recently heard from their clergy about at least one political or social issue.

title: Trading volume on prediction markets has soared in recent months
summary: Prediction market trading volume has risen from under $5 billion monthly in mid 2025 to nearly $24 billion in April 2026, with sports dominating.

10 facts about Americans and marijuana
summary: Nearly nine-in-ten U.S. adults say marijuana should be legal either for medical or recreational use. Just 11% say the drug should not be legal at all.

title: Have Americans’ wages kept up with inflation? That depends
summary: Determining whether workers' wages have kept up with inflation depends on many factors.

title: Key findings about Americans and mental health
summary: As the nation marks Mental Health Awareness Month, here’s a look at how Americans describe their mental health and who they feel comfortable talking to about it.

title: 5 facts about Africa’s population growth
summary: While global population growth is projected to slow over the rest of the century, Africa stands out for its relatively young and growing population.

title: Trump’s approval rating hits second-term low among his Latino voters, though many still approve
summary: About two-thirds of Latino Trump voters (66%) approve of his job performance. That’s down 27 percentage points since the start of his second term.

title: A majority of Americans say the country’s best years are behind us
summary: Americans are also much more pessimistic (44%) than optimistic (28%) when asked to think about what things will be like in the U.S. 50 years from now.

title: What Americans think it takes to be a good news consumer
summary: One of the most common things Americans associate with being a good news consumer is a sense of skepticism or discernment.

title: How Americans Feel About Religion’s Influence in Government and Public Life
summary: A growing share of U.S. adults say religion is gaining influence, but most still want churches to stay out of politics, a 2026 survey finds.

title: Americans See Health Care Costs, Deficit, Inflation as Big Problems Facing the Nation
summary: Economic issues continue to dominate Americans’ ranking of the country's top problems. Meanwhile, the share who say illegal immigration is a very big problem has dropped since the start of Trump’s second term.
